races.name: Ripon Racecourse Ladies' Derby Handicap (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (Special Rider Conditions)

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: In superb form with three consecutive wins including two on Good ground and one on Soft-over-Firm, runs off a low 3-day turnaround suggesting connections are confident; a genuine hold-up horse for whom this 1m4f trip is arguably a stretch of her preferred 1m2f, but her momentum and Tony Carroll's 7/62 14-day strike rate are compelling positives.

runners_data.name: One Million Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up style who has placed three times from 15 Good-ground runs but has not won since 2022; recent form includes a string of finishes outside the frame and headgear (hood) suggests she needs the right setup — this distance of 1m4f is longer than most of her recent entries and her jumping of 12f suggests some stamina questions.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with five placings from 15 Good-ground runs; form shows three consecutive thirds and a second suggesting she runs her race without winning, making her a solid place candidate but one you cannot confidently back to break her losing spell, particularly for an amateur jockey race where tactical nuances matter.

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose true role is pace-setting — her STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 is a reminder that she is racing out of role only in the sense that she is being asked to lead without a challenger, which actually suits her; 83 days off the track is a slight fitness concern, and her best form has come on Tapeta/Polytrack (1 win, 1 place from 15 Good-ground runs) rather than turf going.

runners_data.name: Max Of Stars
runners_data.note: Resurgent after a 265-day layoff backed by a 60-race-experienced jockey and three wins from 16f runs including one on Good ground; a genuine hold-up type whose Ripon 1m4f form is worth checking — his long absence is a risk but the sharp jockey booking (60 rides) hints at a calculated return.

runners_data.name: Bruce Banner
runners_data.note: A natural off-the-pace horse whose deeper hold-up profile has been pushed forward on the map because of field overcrowding — his actual race-day position will likely be towards the rear; has placed twice from 15 runs including seconds at 1m4f on Good and 1m2f on Good, suggesting he stays the trip well enough, though a first win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Bouboule
runners_data.note: Runs in tongue-tie and blinkers, signalling that connections are trying to engineer more co-operation from a hold-up type who has finished outside the frame in all seven lifetime starts — mapped to midfield but will naturally settle in the rear pack; consistent finishing positions in the 7s suggest she lacks a decisive finishing kick, and the amateur context does not help her.

runners_data.name: Arranmore
runners_data.note: A prominent-style runner who is the most natural candidate to sit just behind Jack Langley and the one chaser most likely to actually secure a forward position; has won twice at 1m3f and once at 1m2f on Soft-going, so the Good surface is a possible concern, and her recent form over shorter 1m trips suggests she may need to settle into this longer test.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Carries a finish-fade flag as well as the redistribution note — a genuine hold-up horse placed at the rear but shown in midfield on the map; his form is consistently poor (no wins, no places in last 15 Good-ground runs) and the fade flag compounds concern that even if he travels to a position, he will not sustain his effort to the line.

runners_data.name: Yakhabar
runners_data.note: A hold-up type using tongue-tie and blinkers who has one win and two places from 15 runs in all conditions; recent form shows a 0 (no show) followed by placed finishes, and with a 16-day turnaround he arrives reasonably fresh — at OR 49 he needs everything to fall perfectly, and his natural rear position on the day makes that harder.

runners_data.name: Apache Eagle
runners_data.note: Uses headgear (tongue-tie, hood) and has placed three times in last five runs without winning; a natural hold-up runner whose true race position will be towards the rear despite the midfield mapping, and at OR 46 on the lowest weight (135lbs) he is a potential each-way outsider if the amateur jockey can give him a positive ride at 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Yurinov
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's second runner in this race alongside Speechman, returning after a 96-day absence and racing in a headgear (hood); a consistent midfield-to-rear finisher on Tapeta with no wins or placed finishes on Good ground in his last 15 runs — the layoff and going are twin concerns, and he is likely to need this run to find his best form again.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and will be allowed to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over the 1m4f trip on Good ground at Ripon. With no rival capable of genuinely pressuring him early, the pace is likely to be honest but measured, setting up a test of stamina and finishing power rather than raw speed. The absence of any front-running threat means this race shape is a classically controlled-pace scenario, where the premium shifts to hold-up horses who can travel smoothly and deploy a sustained run from the home turn. True off-the-pace finishers with proven Good-ground form and stamina at this trip — notably Pride Of Nepal, Max Of Stars and Kitsune Power — are best-placed to exploit the steady early tempo and a genuine finish; note also that Bruce Banner, Bouboule, Speechman, Yakhabar, Apache Eagle and Yurinov are all natural hold-up horses mapped forward on the pace map only because the rear of the field is overcrowded, and they are unlikely to all secure prominent positions — Jack Langley and Arranmore are the ones most likely to actually establish forward berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Finishers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the true hold-up horses track through smoothly to deliver their runs from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the true hold-up horses track through smoothly to deliver their runs from the home turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Increase Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Arranmore or a redistributed runner like Bruce Banner pushes forward and forces a more honest middle-mile tempo, lifting the overall pace and stretching the field.
scenarios.body: If Arranmore or a redistributed runner like Bruce Banner pushes forward and forces a more honest middle-mile tempo, lifting the overall pace and stretching the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley is able to steal enough of a break down the back straight and the hold-up horses find themselves unable to close the gap on the Ripon straight.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley is able to steal enough of a break down the back straight and the hold-up horses find themselves unable to close the gap on the Ripon straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late-Race Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the back straight, bunching the field and causing traffic problems on the final bend, producing a muddling finish.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely in the back straight, bunching the field and causing traffic problems on the final bend, producing a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Jack Langley in the early stages — if she is allowed to stride into a comfortable lead down the back, she could prove hard to catch for hold-up horses who find the gallop insufficient to stretch out naturally.

Pride Of Nepal is on a quick three-day turnaround after three consecutive wins; if she shows any sign of staleness or fails to travel with her usual fluency, discount her heavily, as her entire chance rests on a strong late run.

Max Of Stars returns after 265 days off the track — watch the paddock and early market moves carefully, as a ring-rusty performance from such a long layoff would not be surprising despite the experienced jockey booking.

Bruce Banner, Bouboule, Speechman, Yakhabar, Apache Eagle and Yurinov are all genuine hold-up types competing for the same rear-of-field position — traffic and interference on the home bend is a real possibility if several of them switch out simultaneously seeking a run.

Arranmore's ability to sit close to Jack Langley is key to the race shape — if she tracks the leader in second, the race becomes a genuine test of whether the front-runner can be caught; if she drops back, the pace dynamic becomes even more compressed and late finishers gain an additional edge.

races.name: Live For Today Best Dressed Gentleman EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (B/C/D) (Qual') (GBB/IRE Inc')

runners_data.name: Pj's Corner
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Dylan Cunha who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish — sole run was an eighth over 7f on good, suggesting this drop to 6f may help but the closing pattern is a concern; Jason Hart takes the ride for a trainer with 2 wins from 29 runners over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Super Alpha
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston runner lightly raced with a 5th and 3rd to his name on good and soft — unknown early pace style but trip and going are both fine; Connor Beasley is a useful booking and the Johnston yard has hit form (7/50 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Wong Fei Hong
runners_data.note: David O'Meara debutant with no racecourse experience to assess — going and trip preference entirely unknown; Mark Winn takes over and the stable is operating at a solid 9/49 strike rate recently, so should not be underestimated on debut.

runners_data.name: Bigalo
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's hold-up type placed sixth on sole start at 5f on good — the redistribution places him in midfield on the map, but his natural position is further back, which compromises him in a bunched sprint finish; 3/14 for Fell over 14 days, and Oisin McSweeney must find a run.

runners_data.name: Persazz
runners_data.note: William Knight debutant carrying the top weight of 133lbs on debut — no form to assess and going/style both unknown, but the extra weight suggests the stable expects a big performance; Luke Morris is an experienced handler of unknown quantities in these novice conditions.

runners_data.name: Printing Money
runners_data.note: Another Dylan Cunha hold-up type with a last-place run over 6f on good — the fade-in-finish flag makes this a difficult profile in what is likely to be a sprint; Kevin Stott aboard but a ninth on debut gives little basis for optimism.

runners_data.name: Boutblummintime
runners_data.note: Adrian Paul Keatley's Irish raider has two sixth-place finishes on good and soft — a genuine hold-up horse that has been placed into midfield on the map because the rear is congested, dulling its prospects in a shape that already doesn't suit a finisher; Mikey Sheehy will need to find a run in a tight finish.

runners_data.name: Carry On Chaos
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up type has run 9th and 8th in two outings over 6f on good — both runs flagged as fading in the finish, and its true style is rear-group which is compromised by the redistribution to midfield; Duran Fentiman will need clear air that may not materialise.

runners_data.name: Inns And Out
runners_data.note: David Allan partners this Tim Easterby hold-up horse that was fifth over 6f on good last time — running well within its natural range on going and trip, but the congested hold-up group means it must work around rivals rather than drop cleanly in behind; the redistribution to midfield reflects how cramped the back-half of this field will be.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Roger Fell debutant with Joanna Mason booked — like stablemate Bigalo, completely unraced and unknown in terms of style and preference; Mason's local knowledge at Ripon could be an asset if the horse shows any natural early pace.

runners_data.name: State Of Gold
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's hold-up type has run 7th, 5th and 8th in three outings on good ground — the most experienced runner in the field on similar conditions (3 from 3 on good) but the form figures show no upward progression; William Pyle rides and the trainer's 0/9 over 14 days gives little confidence.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in an 11-runner field of juveniles, this 6f contest at Ripon is set to be led by whoever is quickest from the gates rather than a designated pace-setter — the early gallop will be dictated by circumstance rather than intent. The majority of the field are hold-up types by nature, meaning the early pace is likely to be modest and the race will compress into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, favouring horses that can travel prominently or quicken sharply from just off the pace. The field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Inns And Out, Carry On Chaos, Boutblummintime, and Bigalo are all true hold-up types that have been redistributed to midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, meaning their chances are compromised by the congested nature of the rear group. This race shape overwhelmingly favours any horse capable of racing prominently or finding a clean run from midfield in the straight, as the lack of genuine pace and the bunching of hold-up types creates a chaotic finish where clear running lanes will be decisive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Modest Pace Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of a true front-runner produces a crawl early that detonates into a wall-to-wall sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If the lack of a true front-runner produces a crawl early that detonates into a wall-to-wall sprint from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutants Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the lightly-raced or unraced entrants possesses natural early pace and simply outruns the field of modest form horses.
scenarios.body: If one or more of the lightly-raced or unraced entrants possesses natural early pace and simply outruns the field of modest form horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Types Outrun
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is marginally stronger than expected and hold-up horses find a clear run to pick up those who have raced prominently.
scenarios.body: If the pace is marginally stronger than expected and hold-up horses find a clear run to pick up those who have raced prominently.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Shock
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded, leaderless early stages produce scrimmaging and a horse emerges late from the outside to scoop the prize.
scenarios.body: If the crowded, leaderless early stages produce scrimmaging and a horse emerges late from the outside to scoop the prize.

watchPoints.text: Persazz and Johns Power are unraced and their natural gate speed is entirely unknown — either could set or take advantage of the contested early pace and catch the hold-up heavy field off guard.

Inns And Out, Carry On Chaos, Boutblummintime and Bigalo are all genuine hold-up types crammed into a midfield that is already congested — watch for a chain-reaction traffic problem in the straight that could eliminate multiple runners at once.

Super Alpha returns after 53 days off for Charlie Johnston — the layoff is notable in a novice sprint and any race-rustiness from the longer break could see it drop away from a prominent position rather than quickening clear.

State Of Gold is the only runner with three outings on good ground under its belt, giving Craig Lidster's team the clearest going picture — but three runs without a win or place at this level means improved form is needed rather than just a repeat.

Wong Fei Hong and Johns Power are both debut runners from yards with strong recent strike rates (O'Meara 9/49, Fell 3/14) — unknown quantities in a field of exposed modest form horses, and stable confidence on debut should not be dismissed.

races.name: Grantley Hall Handicap

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer who has solid form on Good going but must overcome a tendency to finish mid-pack; Connor Beasley's local knowledge helps, and the 14-day freshness is a mild positive, though the horse's OR-75 mark and recent form string of 747425 suggest limited upside without a truly strong pace to finish into.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner here who shapes as the critical pace-setter; Jason Hart can control every fraction on Good ground, though the horse's Standard-going form record (2/15 similar-going, zero wins) raises a flag about whether Good turf truly suits him, and the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects that his natural role is prominent rather than a true tearaway leader.

runners_data.name: Poet's Dawn
runners_data.note: Veteran 11-year-old with two wins from ten starts on Good going and a best-of-field similar-going record of 10/15; runs in headgear, the six-day turnaround is tight but Tim Easterby's yard is in strong form at T14:8/90, and a prominent style means this horse should be ideally placed throughout if the pace holds at a sustainable level.

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up specialist whose most recent runs have come on Soft ground — the step up to Good may not be a concern but the return to 10f from shorter trips is worth noting; Tim Easterby's eight-year-old is squeezed into a midfield position rather than his preferred rear berth because the field is so hold-up heavy, and the 0.91 style-fit flag tempers confidence in him finding his rhythm.

runners_data.name: What's The Plan
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old from James Fanshawe's yard with a genuine hold-up profile and headgear noted; placed three times in four Good-ground starts (4/7 sim-going, zero wins) and the 26-day absence is manageable, though a 7lb claimer taking the ride on a 130lb-carrying runner in a handicap asks a positional question at a track the horse hasn't visited before.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's three-year-old has an admirable placed record — third in three of five starts on Good or Standard turf — and Mark Winn is a capable booking; a true closer by nature who is pushed into a midfield berth here because of the field's composition, the 0.90 style-fit score and the 22-day freshness combine to make this one to watch for a place rather than a win if the pace stays slow.

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's two-year-old carries the longest absence in the field at 182 days and steps into handicap company from a modest three-run form line all on Standard going; a natural hold-up type remapped to midfield, the unknown quantity angle and complete absence of Good-going evidence make this the most opaque runner in the race, though Prescott's clinical return-day handling is always worth acknowledging.

races.paceDynamic: King Of Fury is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, will control proceedings from the outset at a sustainable, measured gallop over Ripon's 1m2f trip. Poet's Dawn and Qitaal both carry prominent or hold-up profiles but neither is likely to challenge King Of Fury for the lead, leaving him to dictate every fraction unchallenged. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Saxophonist, Roc De Fer, and Yermanthere are all genuine closers who have been mapped into midfield because they cannot all get their natural rearward position, meaning the race will not generate the strong early pace that true closers need. A lone front-runner operating at a controlled tempo over a turning Ripon mile-and-two is a race shape that systematically favours horses able to race prominently or track close to the pace, converting their ground-saving position into a decisive advantage when the sprint home begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Front Two Win
scenarios.trigger: If King Of Fury dictates a steady tempo unchallenged and those racing close to the pace inherit his slipstream into the straight.
scenarios.body: If King Of Fury dictates a steady tempo unchallenged and those racing close to the pace inherit his slipstream into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Lone Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so conservative that King Of Fury simply stretches clear before the field can organise a challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: If the tempo is so conservative that King Of Fury simply stretches clear before the field can organise a challenge in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If King Of Fury sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the race truly plays into the hands of the closers forced into midfield positions.
scenarios.body: If King Of Fury sets a stronger-than-expected pace and the race truly plays into the hands of the closers forced into midfield positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Youth And Freshness Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the younger, lightly-raced horses Roc De Fer or Saxophonist outrun their rivals' experience with raw ability on a clean-run Good surface.
scenarios.body: If the younger, lightly-raced horses Roc De Fer or Saxophonist outrun their rivals' experience with raw ability on a clean-run Good surface.

watchPoints.text: King Of Fury's ability to control fractions is the single biggest variable — if Jason Hart elects to crawl, every hold-up horse in this field is compromised and Poet's Dawn tracking close becomes the play.

Roc De Fer's 182-day absence for Sir Mark Prescott is a known Prescott angle worth monitoring in the market; a significant market move in the minutes before post should be treated seriously given the trainer's record with fresh horses.

Saxophonist, Yermanthere, and Roc De Fer are all genuine closers who cannot occupy their natural rearward positions — if they crowd each other in a compressed midfield group there is a risk of traffic issues in Ripon's turning straight.

What's The Plan, a 3-year-old with a hold-up profile and a 7lb claimer aboard, will need a clear passage from a wide draw and is the most positionally vulnerable runner if the early pace bunches the field.

Good ground is confirmed across all seven Ripon races today with no variation — surface consistency removes going-suitability as a differentiating factor and places premium on positional tactics and draw rather than ground preferences.

races.name: Ripon Races Ladies' Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Strong Warrior
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey's hold-up sprinter returns from 132 days off and carries a worrying tendency to fade in the finish — his best recent effort (2nd, 6f Good) came in a stronger gallop; the layoff combined with his pattern of fading makes him a significant risk even if the race sets up for late runners.

runners_data.name: Dark Cloud Rising
runners_data.note: O'Meara's prominent racer sports a hood and arrives on a 19-day turnaround with a strong trainer in form (10/60, T14); his 6f Good record is poor on paper (one win from 11 attempts on similar going) but his recent run of form figures suggests he finds his level competitively here tracking the pace.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Keatley's six-year-old has won over 5f Good and has course experience, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects that today's prominent tag is a slight role adjustment — his chance depends entirely on being allowed to dictate, which looks near-certain in this field; freshness (12 days since last run) is a mild positive.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Quinn's hold-up performer has an impressive C&D win on his CV (1/6f GOO) and arrives on 18 days' rest — his preferred waiting tactics are genuine but he needs the pace to be robust enough to bring him into it, which this scenario may not fully provide; Jason Hart's booking is a quality addition.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Hannon's prominent filly arrives on just seven days' turnaround with Kevin Stott aboard and a sequence of placed efforts over 6f in varying going — her 0W5P record on similar going is a concern, but she consistently runs to a level and her handy style suits the expected race shape well.

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old is a natural pace-prominent type pushed into a midfield mapping because the field cannot accommodate his preferred position — his STYLE_FIT (0.93) reflects racing out of role, and his best form is over 5f not 6f; the hood (tp) is noted but the combination of trip and compromised berth tempers his prospects.

runners_data.name: Miraculous
runners_data.note: Another Easterby runner, a true hold-up horse who cannot secure his preferred deep position cleanly in this field and carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 — his placings over 6f Good are consistent but not winning, and racing in a position that is not naturally his own on a track where a genuine strong pace is unlikely to develop limits his upside considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Another Baar is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a seven-runner field, is set to control the tempo from the gates on this flat Ripon 6f track — a sustainable, uncontested gallop rather than a scorching one. Dark Cloud Rising and Wild Clary will push forward to track him prominently, creating an orthodox, orderly pace shape that does not collapse early enough to bring hold-up horses into contention from deep. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural berth: Vince L'Amour and Miraculous are genuine pace-prominent and hold-up horses respectively but both are displaced in the map — Vince L'Amour is unlikely to get his natural prominent slot, and Miraculous cannot find its preferred rear-of-field position cleanly. With Good going, a controlled pace, and a short 6f trip, this race shape firmly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can quicken from a handy position without needing a strong gallop to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Another Baar dictates a fair but untaxing pace and horses racing prominently or just off his flank deliver their challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Another Baar dictates a fair but untaxing pace and horses racing prominently or just off his flank deliver their challenge inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Another Baar's uncontested lead allows him to conserve energy and produce a race-winning burst from the front in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Another Baar's uncontested lead allows him to conserve energy and produce a race-winning burst from the front in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and hold-up finishers are able to reel in a flattening field in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and hold-up finishers are able to reel in a flattening field in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses contest the lead aggressively and the whole field compresses entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If multiple prominent horses contest the lead aggressively and the whole field compresses entering the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: Another Baar sets every fraction unchallenged — watch whether he slows the pace through the dip, as a falsely run middle section would dramatically improve hold-up horses Dark Thirty and Strong Warrior at the expense of the prominent brigade.

Dark Cloud Rising's hood suggests some temperament management is ongoing — watch for any signs of restlessness or reluctance at the start, as a tardy break from a prominent horse tracking the pace would materially affect the race shape.

Strong Warrior's 132-day absence is the longest in the field — watch his early movement and condition in the preliminaries; a fit-looking, forward-travelling profile in the parade would elevate his chance, but a flat or laboured warm-up would confirm risk.

Vince L'Amour and Miraculous are both Tim Easterby runners whose natural positions are compromised by this race shape — watch for any pre-race market moves on either, as insider confidence in one could signal a tactical surprise is planned.

Wild Clary's seven-day turnaround is notably quick for a Richard Hannon runner — watch whether she travels with her usual fluency in the early stages, as any signs of staleness or listlessness would undermine what is otherwise a well-suited positional profile.

races.name: Masons Gin 'Who Dares, Gins' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Napoleons Casino And Restaurant Leeds Handicap

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here; Kevin Stott has ridden her into the lead before and she has placed twice on Good going at 6f, though her recent form reads 330-46 and she is arguably racing out of her best role as a P-type who needs to lead rather than track — the sole confirmed pace-setter gives her an uncontested chance to dictate.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has a strong 14-day record (6/89) and David Allan takes the ride; she ran a solid second over 6f on Soft recently, but she is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position simply because the race cannot accommodate all the closers at the back — her late-run angle depends on pace developing generously.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has placed three times from eleven Good-going starts, including a recent second at 6f on Good — a genuinely strong closer by nature whose redistribution to midfield in the map reflects overcrowding of hold-up types rather than her actual preference for racing from the rear.

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this 4yo who has an impressive two wins and three places from fifteen Good-going runs, the best record in the field on this surface; he typically holds up, but his Good-going record makes him the most credible beneficiary if pace does develop strongly enough to let him come through.

runners_data.name: Wish This
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted and won last time out over 6f on Standard; Alan Brown's yard is 0/4 in 14 days which is quiet, and the horse has placed just once on Good in five attempts — a closer by style whose win came on a different surface, making the step to Good ground a mild query.

runners_data.name: Rajstar
runners_data.note: Returns from 124 days off for Ben Haslam, whose stable is 4/13 in 14 days suggesting runners are in form; only one Good-going run in the sample (sixth over 7f) and all recent form is on Standard, so the surface switch combined with the long absence makes this a speculative hold-up runner at best.

runners_data.name: Federal Envoy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine is 0/17 in the 14-day window — a significant stable flag — and this 5yo has all five recent runs on Standard going, never racing on Good in the recorded history; a true hold-up horse by style, mapped to midfield through redistribution, with minimal evidence of Good-ground suitability.

runners_data.name: Fircombe Hall
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's 8yo wears a hood and has two recent seconds at 6f over Standard, placing once in fifteen Good-going attempts — his prominent style makes him the most natural companion to Liosa at the head of affairs, and at OR 54 he carries the lightest weight, which could matter in a race that sets up for those on the pace.

races.paceDynamic: Liosa is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 6f Ripon handicap and, with Fircombe Hall the only other prominent-style runner, she faces minimal early pressure and can set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front. On Good ground over this flat six furlongs, an uncontested lead is a significant asset, allowing Liosa and Fircombe Hall to dictate fractions and preserve energy for the finish rather than burning it in an opening battle. The field behind is dominated by hold-up horses — Fan Mail, Big Apple Jack, Rajstar, and Federal Envoy are all genuine closers who have been redistributed into the midfield map position simply because the race does not have room for all of them at the rear; they are unlikely to secure anything more forward than they naturally want to be, and with no one to seriously press the front end, their challenge depends on a truly strong late surge. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — specifically Liosa and Fircombe Hall — as a controlled pace on Good ground at a flat sprint track historically rewards those who travel close to the action and don't have ground to make up in the straight.

scenarios.title: Liosa Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Liosa bowls along uncontested and Fircombe Hall tracks closely, setting a fair but not extreme pace.
scenarios.body: If Liosa bowls along uncontested and Fircombe Hall tracks closely, setting a fair but not extreme pace.

scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the first 3f to compress the final-furlong margins and allow the back-of-the-field runners to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough through the first 3f to compress the final-furlong margins and allow the back-of-the-field runners to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises on Chaos

scenarios.body: If the field bunches badly at some point, causing interference or a tactical reshuffle that lets a lower-rated runner find a clean passage at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Liosa and Fircombe Hall — if either drifts or the pair meet trouble from the gates, the single confirmed lead is gone and the race shape collapses entirely, opening it to the hold-up pack.
Mr Cool — with the best Good-going record in the field (2W/3P from 15 runs), any sign of him travelling smoothly in the straight should be taken seriously even from a hold-up position.

Fan Mail — David Allan is a strong claimer around here and the horse's Soft-ground second shows she can perform; if the pace is stronger than anticipated, her redistribution to midfield could accidentally place her in an advantageous position.

Rajstar — 124 days off combined with a trainer firing in-form (4/13 T14) is a combination worth monitoring in the market; significant drifting or support either way is informative about stable confidence on the return.

Federal Envoy — the 0/17 trainer 14-day stat alongside a complete absence of Good-going form flags this runner as one to monitor for market weakness; any market move would be surprising and worth noting.

races.name: Your Harrogate Ladies' Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here; Tim Easterby's filly can dictate from the front on good going but her recent form reads mostly 5th-6th, and racing over a mile for the first time stretches her stamina credentials — the lone lead is a tactical gift but the form ceiling is modest.

runners_data.name: Lc Tiffen
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has struggled to land a blow in seven runs, zero wins or placings on good ground in similar company; Rhys Elliott takes off 5lb but the trainer's 14-day record of 0 from 4 offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Spirit
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's filly returns after 66 days off, a significant freshener to note; she races from the back and has shown only one run on similar going in her recent history — market confidence after the break would be telling.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: The standout form angle — won last time at seven furlongs on good going and has four of her last five runs on good or similar ground; Tony Carroll sends her here fresh off a 10-day turnaround and her hold-up style suits a truly-run mile.

runners_data.name: Raven's View
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse who steps sharply back in trip from 10-12f recent starts — her form at shorter distances is limited and the redistribution to midfield reflects the congested rear of this field, not a shift in her racing pattern.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Mary
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is a significant concern in a race likely to produce a searching late test; dropped in trip from her recent starts and her Alex Jary 3lb claim is the most obvious positive in a limited profile.

runners_data.name: Hood Wink
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places on good going over eight furlongs, making her the most course-appropriate hold-up runner in the field; blinkers are fitted and she races for in-form Tim Easterby (10 wins from 113 in 14 days) — the style-fit discount is worth noting but her going and trip record stand out.

runners_data.name: Trucial Pearl
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride on this visor-wearing hold-up filly who has placed on good ground over seven furlongs; consistent without winning, her 0 wins from 11 good-ground runs is a concern but she finds herself near the bottom of the weights.

runners_data.name: Regal Knight
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this hold-up type who carries headgear (p) and has placings over eight and ten furlongs on good ground; the trainer combination of Coyle & Wood has 0 wins from 12 runners in the past 14 days — needs things to fall perfectly.

races.paceDynamic: Hatamoto is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner mile handicap at Ripon, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on good ground. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Raven's View, A Boy Named Mary, Hood Wink, Trucial Pearl, and Regal Knight are all natural rear-end horses redistributed toward midfield on the map simply because five true closers cannot all occupy the back of the field simultaneously in a nine-runner race. Shes Got The Blues, Lc Tiffen, and Shimmering Spirit add further hold-up weight, meaning there is almost no genuine mid-division pressure to stretch Hatamoto's comfortable lead. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone uncontested front-runner setting a moderate pace on flat, good ground at a one-mile track favours horses who can race prominently or pick up off a sound but unspectacular tempo — genuine hold-up types off a slow burn have limited room to generate the momentum needed to run down a fresh, unharried leader.

scenarios.trigger: If Hatamoto's uncontested lead produces a falsely slow early gallop that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Hatamoto's uncontested lead produces a falsely slow early gallop that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish from the home turn.

watchPoints.text: Shes Got The Blues arrives here on the back of a win just 10 days ago — watch whether Tony Carroll's sharp turnaround leaves her as sharp as on that winning day or slightly blunted.
With five or more true hold-up types forced toward midfield on the map, watch for a congested home straight if Hatamoto dawdles early — a bunched finish could produce bumping or interference.
Hood Wink wears blinkers and has Tim Easterby's strong recent strike rate behind her — watch for her being sent forward earlier than her redistribution position implies if the pace is slow.
Shimmering Spirit has had 66 days off — watch the market in the final 30 minutes for any stable support that would indicate she has been readied for this comeback run.

A Boy Named Mary is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — watch whether she is placed aggressively early by Alex Jary to compensate, which would alter the pace dynamic if she gets closer to Hatamoto than expected.
